blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A loader runs `int i = 0; slots[i] = i++ + 10;` on a new `int[] slots = new int[3]`. Which element of `slots` is set, and to what?

options.text: slots[0] is 10, since the index is read while i is still 0 and i++ yields 0
options.says: the left operand of the assignment, the index, is evaluated first, and i++ has the old value, 0

options.text: slots[1] is 10, since i++ runs before the index is read and i++ yields 0
options.says: operands run left to right, so the index is read as 0 before i++ runs

options.text: slots[0] is 11, since the index is read while i is still 0 and i++ yields 1
options.says: i++ has the old value, 0, so the sum is 10

options.text: slots[1] is 11, since i++ runs before the index is read and i++ yields 1
options.says: the index is read first, and i++ has the old value

origin.section: Precedence and Associativity Group an Expression; Its Operands Still Run Left to Right

questions.stem: A retry loop logs `"attempt " + attempt + 1 + " of " + max` with `attempt` at 2 and `max` at 5. What text is logged?

options.text: attempt 3 of 5, since attempt + 1 is added as two ints first and the sum is then joined to the text
options.says: + groups left to right, so attempt is joined to "attempt " before 1 is reached

options.text: attempt 21 of 5, since "attempt " + attempt is joined first and 1 is then joined to that text
options.says: + groups left to right; once the left operand is a String, + 1 appends "1"

options.text: attempt 3 of 5, since the + between two int operands binds tighter than the + that joins text
options.says: addition and concatenation are the same operator with one precedence

options.text: attempt 21 of 5, since the + that joins text binds tighter than the + between two int operands
options.says: addition and concatenation have the same precedence; the result comes from left-to-right grouping (10 + 20 + " items" adds first)

origin.section: Precedence and Associativity Group an Expression; Its Operands Still Run Left to Right

questions.stem: A scheduler names a past weekday with `DAYS[(today - back) % 7]`. With `today` at 2 and `back` at 10, what index does the expression inside the brackets produce?

options.text: -1, since the remainder takes the sign of the left operand, -8
options.says: Java defines % so that (a / b) * b + a % b == a with / truncating toward zero, which gives the remainder the dividend's sign: -8 % 7 is -1, and DAYS[-1] throws

options.text: 6, since the remainder takes the sign of the right operand, 7
options.says: that is Math.floorMod; % takes the sign of the dividend, -8

options.text: -1, since % rounds the quotient -8 / 7 down to -2 before taking the remainder
options.says: integer / truncates toward zero, to -1, not down; and a quotient of -2 would leave a remainder of 6, not -1

options.text: 6, since % rounds the quotient -8 / 7 toward zero to -1 before taking the remainder

origin.section: Integer Division Truncates Toward Zero, and % Takes the Sign of the Dividend

questions.stem: A permissions table gets a new entry with `long mask = 1 << 33;`. What value does `mask` hold?

options.text: 8589934592, since the long on the left of = makes the shift a 64-bit one
options.says: only the left operand sets a shift's type; 1 is an int, and the result is widened only after the shift

options.text: 8589934592, since a distance above 31 makes the int shift a 64-bit one
options.says: nothing widens the left operand; an int shift uses only the low five bits of its distance

options.text: 2, since an int shift keeps only the low five bits of its distance
options.says: 33 & 31 is 1, so 1 << 33 is 1 << 1, and 2 is then widened to long

options.text: 0, since an int shift drops any bit that moves past bit 31
options.says: the distance is reduced to its low five bits first, so the bit never moves past bit 31

origin.section: Bit Operators Bind Looser Than ==, and an int Shift Counts Only to 31

concepts: + groups left to right, and once its left operand is a String it concatenates, so "s" + 1 + 2 is "s12" while 1 + 2 + "s" is "3s".
Precedence decides grouping, not the order of evaluation: Java evaluates the left operand fully before the right one, including an array index on the left of an assignment.
x++ evaluates to the old value and increments as a side effect, so x = x++ leaves x unchanged.
